Milestone 3's core: the coach comments on chosen aspects of a position, never sees what would spoil a game in progress, can comment by itself, and has every move it names checked.

- **Aspects and templates (TODO 3.2, 3.3):**

  - legal moves outside the engine's lines are greyed out as unchecked;
  - wrong "piece on square" claims are counted;

- **Cache (3.7):** keyed by position, move, aspects, engine view, level and model. It survives reloads; a cached comment shows "(saved)".

Base: `main`. Merging this PR puts it on `main`.

## What and why

The coach can now run without a network, a key or a provider. A small model runs inside the page.

- **`just offline`:**
  - The first run downloads Qwen2.5 1.5B Instruct (1.1 GB, Apache-2.0; `just offline qwen2.5-0.5b` for 0.5 GB) into `site/models/` and checks its SHA-256 against a pinned catalog.
  - Then it serves without `.env` keys, in local-only mode, and the page requests nothing from other hosts: no Google Fonts, and a CSP that allows no other host.
- **Runtime:** wllama 3.8.1 (MIT, llama.cpp) runs the model on WebGPU, or in multi-threaded WebAssembly on the CPU. `src/browser-llm.js`:
  - loads it only after the player presses Load, with progress;
  - streams and cancels answers, and runs one request at a time;
  - unloads after ten idle minutes and checks memory first;
  - loads the model into memory when browser storage is too small.
- **Gateway:** a local `browser` provider. The status says where the weights are, but the gateway never runs the model. `serve.mjs --models` serves only the catalog's files. A downloaded model also shows up under `just serve` as "In browser".
- **Routing (2.16.5):** a setting sends only quick requests (chips, coach comments) to the in-browser model, and the rest to the configured provider.
- **Shared CPU (2.16.4):** while the model generates on the CPU, Stockfish's analyst gets fewer threads.

pulls.body:
Base: `main`. Merging this PR puts it on `main`. Docs only.

## What and why

`docs/ARCH.md` explains how Kibitz is built and why:

1. **The idea:** a symbolic engine (Stockfish, chess.js, the motif detectors) calculates and checks, and a language model explains. The symbolic side has the last word. This is also the user experience: numbers come from the engine, help is a dial, and trust is visible in the answers.
2. **Where things run:** the page, the local server and gateway, the providers, with a Mermaid diagram. Also the artifact and offline deployments.
3. **Generative-AI patterns as built here,** each pointing to the code:
   - context control;
   - retrieval (RAG);

ESLint's lexical scope manager supplies direct `calls` and read `references_binding`; declared local exports supply `imports_binding`. Source modules are never executed. Shadowed parameters and reassigned/multiply-defined bindings do not become guessed function targets.

## PR provenance

`utils/assure-detail.mjs` provides `refreshPullRequests` and `validatePullRequests`. `docs/assure/pull-requests.json` retains public PR bodies, observed states, exact head/base commits and paginated file lists. Each PR description section has its own identity, source range and hash. Explicit TODO/file/name references connect sections to planning items, files and unambiguous objects. File changes remain a separate `changes_file` relation. Normal build/check/viewing is offline; only explicit `just assure-prs` uses read-only GitHub metadata access.

## Documentation

`utils/assure-detail.mjs` extracts `sections` into separate `docs/assure/documents.json`: ATX/setext headings, duplicate anchors, hierarchy, fenced blocks, inline/full/collapsed reference links, local section targets and HTTP(S) documentation URLs. `locates_item` retains links to original TODO/DONE/insight/deviation nodes. External documentation is indexed without fetching its contents. `docs/assure/detail-types.mjs` uses `validateLayers` to check the shared schema, endpoint types, ownership and level-1 snapshot identity.

## Browser

`utils/assure-browser/model.mjs` supplies `indexGraph`, `search` and `walk`; `utils/assure-browser/serve.mjs` implements `createBrowser`. Run **`just assure-browser`**, then open the printed loopback URL. The viewer offers text/ID search, level/type/relation filters, incoming/outgoing walks, bounded depth, graph and keyboard-accessible list navigation, history/deep links, gap details and hash-checked source inspection. Search and traversal disclose their 100-result/70-node limits.

[Foundation comparison](docs/assure/LEVELS.md#browser-foundation-comparison): choose exact development dependency Cytoscape.js **3.34.4**, MIT, over Graphology + Sigma for this bounded viewer. It is served locally from the locked npm package with its licence; no CDN or vendored bundle. It is not copied into the chess app or runtime image. The utility supplies Cytoscape's fixed container rule from local CSS, preserving a self-only script/stylesheet policy; runtime canvas style attributes are permitted only in this utility. The chess app's policy is unchanged.

## Limits

These are reference-granularity levels, not proof-strength levels. Mentions/changes do not establish implementation, test success, compliance, completion or approval. Object mentions require an exact name plus a cited file in the same authored section/item; incomplete historical descriptions are not backfilled by guessing. PR descriptions are retained snapshots, not immutable GitHub body revisions. Dynamic/member calls, external package targets, re-export chains, unsupported languages, custom HTML/shortcut anchors and runtime execution remain outside extraction; exclusions and unresolved references are explicit. TODO checkbox state remains the sole planning-status source.

- Full unit/server suite: **720 passes, one opt-in live skip**. All **21 focused assurance fixtures** pass, including eight new object/document/PR cases.
- **Three focused Playwright cases pass**, exercising actual viewer search/filter/source/direction/history/deep-link/truncation behavior, hostile text, source-ID/path confinement, Host/method checks and CSP. No external browser request, page error or CSP violation occurs. Visual inspection checks readable labels and directed layout.
- Independent fixtures cover shadowed lexical names, imported exports, callbacks, inline HTML offsets, non-code scripts, commented/string fake declarations, duplicate/setext headings, literal fences, reference links, absent anchors, ambiguity, deterministic ordering, replay drift, malformed types/endpoints/ownership and bounded directed walks.

pulls.body:
## What and why

TODO 0.17: assurance links need confidence in their particular relationship type so we can investigate evidence gaps and deviations without turning file mentions into implementation claims. Add confidence across all three graph levels, editable type assessments, deterministic findings and browser inspection. Expand `docs/assure/README.md` into the entry point for the model, examples and maintenance.

This main-targeted PR includes prerequisite #137 (which includes #136). Merge those first to narrow the final diff. No automatic merge, release, tag or publication is requested.

## Typed confidence

`docs/assure/confidence.mjs` implements `confidence`, `classifyLink` and `pathConfidence`. Extracted graph schemas advance to version 2 and require every edge to carry a finite [0,1] weight, method, policy and rationale. Direct syntactic/structural support scores 1; unique suffix resolution scores 0.8; constrained object-name attribution scores 0.85. These are transparent, uncalibrated support conventions for the declared type, not probabilities of endpoint truth, requirement satisfaction or defects.

`docs/assure/assessment-types.mjs` implements `validateAssessments` and `applyAssessments`. Editable `docs/assure/links.json` can add `implements`, `verifies`, `documents`, `deviates_from`, `supports` and `contradicts`, or override confidence for an existing extracted type/pair. Different types can coexist for the same pair; they are not normalized. Overrides preserve extracted provenance and remove the original stronger weight from the effective graph. Analysts cannot invent parsed containment or static-call edges. Two seed author hypotheses connect this utility and its fixtures to TODO 0.17; neither asserts independent acceptance or successful execution.

## Findings and inference

`utils/assure-infer.mjs` implements `inferFindings` and `findingReport`. Separate generated `docs/assure/findings.json` and `FINDINGS.md` distinguish:

- Recorded authored deviations and proposed deviation assessments.
- Unresolved references and checked TODOs lacking a DONE annotation link.
- Unassessed implementation/verification evidence, which does not prove code/tests are absent.
- Competing support/contradiction assessments.
- Possible dependency impact through an explicit implementation/deviation association and bounded incoming static dependencies, which identifies review scope rather than an observed defect or cause.

Each supported finding retains typed edges and weights. Path support uses the minimum; alternatives use the maximum, without multiplying probabilities or assuming independence. Repeated evidence and cycles cannot inflate support; stronger alternate paths remain usable. Defaults are threshold 0.8, depth 2 and at most 100 impact nodes per deviation context, with truncation explicit. Identical unresolved citations are deduplicated; raw extractor records remain available. Reports escape HTML and Markdown link syntax.

## Browser and README

`utils/assure-browser/model.mjs` filters `walk` by minimum confidence; the browser shows weighted edges, confidence rationales and original/assessment citations. A searchable findings panel distinguishes recorded observations, trace gaps and review candidates and exposes support paths. Findings use their stated rule threshold independently of the graph display filter. The read-only server constructs the effective graph from validated snapshots/assessments offline.

`docs/assure/README.md` now documents all three levels, their files/contracts, relation families, confidence policy, editable examples, every inference rule, aggregation and negative-evidence limits, browser usage and deterministic rebuild/check procedures. `just assure-build`, `just assure` and CI include the findings and assessment schema. Generated reports are excluded from input scanning to avoid recursive hashes.

## Validation

- Node 24.22.1: normal lint/JSDoc/ASVS, expanded utility lint and exact graph/finding freshness pass; fresh application build passes.
- Full unit/server suite: **730 passes, one opt-in live skip**.
- **31 focused assurance fixtures**, including ten new confidence/inference cases: numeric bounds and non-finite values, constrained types/endpoints, confidence overrides versus parallel types, no invented extracted links, no promotion of mentions/status into implementation, threshold-sensitive evidence gaps, authored/combined rationale boundaries, source locations, bounded propagation, cycles/repeated evidence/stronger paths, competing hypotheses and safe report text.
- **Four real-browser tests** pass: existing search/source/history/security cases plus actual confidence filtering, weight/rationale inspection, findings search and typed support paths.
- No new dependency, provider call, weight download or operator environment inspection. The app's chess, prompt, state and CSP behavior are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Meaningful Node fixtures and real-browser coverage
- [x] Local check, build and full unit suite pass; focused viewer tests pass
- [x] TODO 0.17 ticked; DONE records implementation, deviations and insights
- [x] No additional dependency

## Security impact

- [x] All confidence values validated, including NaN/infinity/range rejection
- [x] Authored assessments require valid typed endpoints, analyst rationale and a repository citation
- [x] Untrusted finding text remains text in the browser and is escaped in Markdown reports
- [x] Offline, tracked public artifacts only; no API keys or inference calls
- [x] Existing loopback/Host/fixed-asset/source-ID boundaries retained
- [x] No confidence value or derived candidate establishes acceptance, compliance or release approval
